summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of stroke, tracheostomy, G-tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted due to a cracked PEG tube that prevented tube feeding. He had no acute symptoms but presented with leukocytosis and a positive urine culture for Proteus mirabilis. Given his stable condition and lack of infection signs, antibiotics were deferred. The PEG tube was successfully replaced, and his Foley catheter was changed to reduce future infection risk. His white blood cell count improved, and chronic conditions including diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and neuropathic pain were managed. He remained DNR/DNI throughout and was discharged to extended care with no medication changes and wound care instructions for a sacral pressure ulcer.
